_comment: Single authority for the gallery cache builder (L-098 Phase 1b). Seed = the 11-object tranche. slug/horizons_id/id_type/canonical_center/center_slug/parent/canonical_frame/features carried from export_orbit_cache.py TEST_OBJECTS @ orrery 4e2629c; trace_policy is MODEL-derived (conic model: none for every non-spacecraft, full-arc only for spacecraft) and is NOT the retired Stage-2 serve/none field. canonical_center is the Horizons fetch center; center_slug (== stored_center) is the served frame slug. An entry may carry "serve_positions": false (L-234, 2026-08-24): it is served for its features only, no Horizons fetch is made for it, and its canonical_frame keeps it out of the served_window participants. The Sun is the first such entry. info_url on every drawable feature (and the belt info_urls) curated 2026-09-03 (L-265, with Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1): NASA page where one is specific to the feature, else English Wikipedia; the served feature_configs.json / coverage_index.json copies follow on the next builder run.

objects.name: Sun
objects._comment: The scene origin of a heliocentric cache: no orbit is fetched for it, and it is excluded from the served_window participants by canonical_frame. It is here for its shell geometry. Groups mirror the orrery GUI panel (Sun Structures / Solar Atmosphere Structures / Solar Wind Structures / Oort Cloud Structures / Hill Sphere Structure). Custom geometry -- streamer belt, Hills cloud torus, clumpy outer Oort, galactic tide -- is NOT here; it needs the solar pole first (L-229) and its own renderers.

core.name: Core
core.source: Bahcall, Pinsonneault & Basu (2001), ApJ 555:990 (radial profiles); drawn at the low end of the conventional 0.2-0.25 R_sun core range

radiative.name: Radiative Zone
radiative.source: Christensen-Dalsgaard, Gough & Thompson (1991), ApJ 378:413, "The depth of the solar convection zone" -- convection-zone depth measured at 0.287 +/- 0.003 solar radii, so the base of the zone sits at 1 - 0.287 = 0.713 R_sun

photosphere.name: Photosphere
photosphere.source: IAU 2015 Resolution B3 -- nominal solar radius

sun_radius.source: IAU 2015 Resolution B3 -- nominal solar radius

streamer_belt.name: Streamer Belt (helmet and stalk)

cusp_radius.source: Suess and Nerney (2004) -- extent of the closed-field helmet, not of the streamer as a whole

fade_radius.source: Kasper et al. (2021), Phys. Rev. Lett. 127:255101 -- the band dissolves across the Alfven surface

drawing._declared: Every value in this block is a drawing choice, not a measurement. Nobody has sourced the warp amplitude, the lobe count or the widths, and the hover says so to the reader. Copied from planet_visualization_utilities.py::STREAMER_BAND_DEFAULTS.

streamer_belt.note: One configuration near solar minimum. That the belt is organized about the solar equator AT ALL is a drawing choice, not a sourced boundary: the pole is sourced, anchoring the band to it is ours.

chromosphere.name: Chromosphere (2,000 km skin)
chromosphere.source: Carroll & Ostlie, An Introduction to Modern Astrophysics, Ch. 11 -- chromosphere extends about 2000 km above the photosphere
chromosphere.note: Derived: 1 + 2000 km / 695700 km. The sourced claim is the 2000 km thickness, not the ratio. Drawn at true physical scale since 2026-08-16.

inner_corona.name: Inner Corona
inner_corona.source: Lamy, Gilardy, Llebaria, Quemerais & Ernandez, "Coronal Photopolarimetry with the LASCO-C3 Coronagraph over 24 Years [1996-2019]", Solar Physics (arXiv:2009.04820) -- the inner solar corona taken as extending to about 3 R_sun from the center of the solar disk. A stated convention, not a measurement: the inner (K-)corona has no sharp edge, and 3 R_sun is the top of the 2-3 R_sun band across which the F-corona overtakes it in brightness

roche_limit.name: Roche Limit (Comets)
roche_limit.source: Murray & Dermott, Solar System Dynamics (1999), Sec. 4.6

alfven_surface.name: Alfven Surface
alfven_surface.source: Kasper et al. (2021), Phys. Rev. Lett. 127:255101 -- first Parker Solar Probe crossing, 28 April 2021

outer_corona.name: Outer Corona
outer_corona.source: Mann et al. (2004), A&A 414:1127; F-corona envelope, not a sharp physical edge

sun_radius.source: IAU 2015 Resolution B3 -- nominal solar radius

termination_shock.name: Termination Shock
termination_shock.source: Stone et al. (2005), Science 309:2017 -- Voyager 1 crossing at 94 AU

sun_radius.source: IAU 2015 Resolution B3 -- nominal solar radius

hills_cloud_torus.name: Hills Cloud (torus)

outer_radius.source: Hills (1981) -- outer edge of the inner (Hills) cloud

drawing._declared: Drawing choices, not measurements. Copied from solar_visualization_shells.py::create_sun_hills_cloud_torus defaults.

hills_cloud_torus.note: Disk-like rather than spherical: the inner Oort cloud is flattened toward the ecliptic, unlike the outer cloud. The thickness is a drawing choice.

outer_oort_clumpy.name: Outer Oort Cloud (clumps)

inner_radius.source: Hills (1981) -- outer edge of the inner (Hills) cloud

drawing._declared: Drawing choices, not measurements. No survey has resolved individual Oort clumps; the count, sizes and concentration are illustrative of the fact that the cloud is not smooth. Copied from solar_visualization_shells.py::create_sun_outer_oort_clumpy defaults.

outer_oort_clumpy.note: The clumping is illustrative. That the cloud is lumpy is expected from stellar perturbations; where the lumps are is not known and is not claimed here.

galactic_tide.name: Galactic Tide (thinned at the plane)

typical_radius.source: DECLARED -- a mid-cloud distance between the Hills cloud and the outer edge, chosen for the illustration. Not a measurement.

drawing._declared: Drawing choices, not measurements. The radial spread, the clip and the strength of the plane asymmetry are all illustrative.

galactic_tide.note: Objects are drawn thinned near the galactic plane, where the Milky Way's tide is most disruptive. The shape of the asymmetry is illustrative, not fitted to a survey.

inner_oort.name: Inner Oort Cloud
inner_oort.source: Hills (1981) -- outer edge of the inner (Hills) cloud

orientation.source: IAU 2018 (Archinal et al.), solar north pole in ICRF equatorial coordinates
orientation.note: Read by the same poleBasis() the gas giants use; the solar equator sits about 7.25 degrees off the ecliptic.

gravitational.name: Gravitational Influence
gravitational.source: Approximate Hill sphere of the Sun in the Milky Way (model-dependent); literature estimates range 100,000-200,000 AU

objects.name: Earth
objects._comment: L-291 (2026-09-07): entry rebuilt in the measured shape. Every rendered number carries value/unit/source/orrery_constant and is the orrery store's exact value at 5aed0590; the live store-drift run checks each by name. Groups earth_geostationary and earth_magnetosphere have no renderer yet (step 3) and the dispatch says so. Earth-Moon Lagrange points are L-297 and are not here.

inner_core.name: Inner Core
inner_core.source: Dziewonski & Anderson (1981), Preliminary Reference Earth Model, Phys. Earth Planet. Inter. 25:297

outer_core.name: Outer Core
outer_core.source: Dziewonski & Anderson (1981), Preliminary Reference Earth Model, Phys. Earth Planet. Inter. 25:297

lower_mantle.name: Lower Mantle
lower_mantle.source: Ishii, Kumagai, Sugiura & Tsuchiya (2019), Nature Geoscience 12:869 -- the 660-km discontinuity

upper_mantle.name: Upper Mantle
upper_mantle.source: Dziewonski & Anderson (1981), Preliminary Reference Earth Model, Phys. Earth Planet. Inter. 25:297 -- Moho

crust.name: Crust
crust.source: IERS Conventions (2010), Petit & Luzum (eds.), IERS Technical Note No. 36, Table 1.1 -- equatorial radius
crust.note: Drawn at the equatorial radius. Crust thickness (5-10 km oceanic, 30-50 km continental) is below the drawn resolution.

planet_radius.source: IERS Conventions (2010), Petit & Luzum (eds.), IERS Technical Note No. 36, Table 1.1

lower_atmosphere.name: Lower Atmosphere (to the stratopause)
lower_atmosphere.source: NOAA JetStream, "Layers of the Atmosphere"; NASA, "Earth's Atmospheric Layers" -- stratopause at about 50 km
lower_atmosphere.note: Troposphere and stratosphere, 99% of atmospheric mass. Drawn at the physical boundary since 2026-09-07 (L-295); before that at a visibility fraction its own hover contradicted.

upper_atmosphere.name: Upper Atmosphere (to the thermopause)
upper_atmosphere.source: NOAA JetStream, "Layers of the Atmosphere"; NASA, "Earth's Atmospheric Layers" -- thermosphere to about 600 km
upper_atmosphere.note: Mesosphere and thermosphere. The thermopause moves with solar activity over roughly 500-1,000 km; 600 km is the nominal figure.

planet_radius.source: IERS Conventions (2010), Petit & Luzum (eds.), IERS Technical Note No. 36, Table 1.1

geocorona.name: Exosphere / Geocorona (hydrogen halo, detected extent)
geocorona.source: Baliukin, Bertaux, Quemerais, Izmodenov & Schmidt (2019), J. Geophys. Res. Space Physics 124:861, doi:10.1029/2018JA026136 -- the hydrogen geocorona is detected to at least 100 Earth radii
geocorona.note: The exosphere has no boundary: it thins into space. This shell is the sourced DETECTION FLOOR, not an edge, and it encloses the Moon's orbit at about 60 Earth radii. The orrery folds the exosphere into its upper-atmosphere hover; growing it a shell of its own is L-292.

planet_radius.source: IERS Conventions (2010), Petit & Luzum (eds.), IERS Technical Note No. 36, Table 1.1

leo_inner.name: Low Earth Orbit, inner edge (200 km)
leo_inner.source: Drawing floor: the LEO region begins at the surface (IADC-02-01 Rev. 3); 200 km marks where orbits stop decaying within days. Declared, not measured.

leo_outer.name: Low Earth Orbit, outer edge (2,000 km)
leo_outer.source: IADC Space Debris Mitigation Guidelines, IADC-02-01 Rev. 3 (June 2021), sec. 3.3.2 -- the LEO Protected Region extends to 2,000 km altitude

planet_radius.source: IERS Conventions (2010), Petit & Luzum (eds.), IERS Technical Note No. 36, Table 1.1

geostationary_ring.name: Geostationary Belt (GEO)
geostationary_ring.source: Derived: (GM_E / omega^2)^(1/3) from IERS Conventions (2010) TN36 Table 1.1 -- GM_E = 3.986004418e14 m^3 s^-2, nominal mean angular velocity 7.292115e-5 rad s^-1
geostationary_ring.note: A ring in the equatorial plane, not a sphere, tilted with Earth's equator by the served pole. 42,164 km from Earth's centre, 35,786 km up.

planet_radius.source: IERS Conventions (2010), Petit & Luzum (eds.), IERS Technical Note No. 36, Table 1.1

earth_magnetosphere._comment: The orrery emits magnetopause, bow shock, inner belt and outer belt from ONE call. Served as four rows: the two standoffs here, the two belts in van_allen_belts. Renderer for the standoff shapes is step 3.

magnetopause.name: Magnetopause (sunward standoff)
magnetopause.source: Shue et al. (1998), J. Geophys. Res. 103:17691, doi:10.1029/98JA01103 -- r0 = 10.2 R_E at Bz = 0 nT, Dp = 2 nPa; Lugaz et al. (2016), doi:10.1038/ncomms13001 -- typical subsolar magnetopause 9-11 R_E
magnetopause.note: Quiet-time nominal. Under storm compression it can fall inside geostationary orbit (6.6 R_E).

bow_shock.name: Bow Shock (sunward standoff)
bow_shock.source: Lugaz et al. (2016), Nat. Commun. 7:13001, doi:10.1038/ncomms13001 -- under normal solar wind the bow shock forms at 11-14 R_E subsolar. Drawn at the midpoint of that range.
bow_shock.note: Model form: Farris & Russell (1994), J. Geophys. Res. 99:17681. The orrery drew 15 R_E (textbook) until 2026-09-07; store and shells now agree.

magnetotail._declared: Drawing parameters, not measurements: the orrery's tail is drawn to 100 Earth radii with a 15-radius base and 25-radius end; the real tail extends past 1,000 radii and the hover must say so (Show the Envelope).

planet_radius.source: IERS Conventions (2010), Petit & Luzum (eds.), IERS Technical Note No. 36, Table 1.1

inner_belt_distance.source: Baker et al. (2018), Space Sci. Rev. 214:17, doi:10.1007/s11214-017-0452-7 -- inner-zone proton fluxes peak near r ~ 1.5 R_E
inner_belt_distance.note: A flux PEAK, not an edge; the inner belt spans roughly L = 1.1 to 2.

outer_belt_distance.source: J. Geophys. Res. Space Physics (2025), doi:10.1029/2024JA033504 -- the outer belt is most intense around L = 4 and 5; Kellerman et al. (2014) as cited in arXiv:1809.00902 -- maximum electron flux at L = 4-5. Drawn at the midpoint.
outer_belt_distance.note: A flux PEAK, not an edge; the outer belt spans roughly L = 3 to 7 and moves with geomagnetic activity.

van_allen_belts._declared: belt_thickness, n_rings, n_points, colours and names are drawing choices.

planet_radius.source: IERS Conventions (2010), Petit & Luzum (eds.), IERS Technical Note No. 36, Table 1.1

hill_sphere.name: Hill Sphere (gravitational dominance over the Sun)
hill_sphere.source: Derived: r_H = a (GM_E / 3 GM_Sun)^(1/3) with a = 1 AU; GM_E from IERS Conventions (2010) TN36 Table 1.1, GM_Sun from IAU 2015 Resolution B3
hill_sphere.note: About 1.50 million km. The Moon at about 60 Earth radii sits well inside it, which is why it stays bound. a = 1 AU exactly; Earth's semi-major axis is 1.00000011 AU (NASA Earth Fact Sheet).

planet_radius.source: IERS Conventions (2010), Petit & Luzum (eds.), IERS Technical Note No. 36, Table 1.1

orientation.source: IAU 2018 (Archinal et al.) -- Earth's north pole is the J2000 celestial north pole in ICRF equatorial coordinates
orientation.note: Same shape as the Sun's orientation block; read by poleBasis(). The equator plane and the GEO ring both hang off this.

planet_radius.source: IAU 2015 Resolution B3 -- nominal jovian equatorial radius

pole.source: IAU WGCCRE, Archinal et al. 2018, Celest. Mech. Dyn. Astron. 130:22, Table 1
IAU WGCCRE, Archinal et al. 2018, Celest. Mech. Dyn. Astron. 130:22, Table 1

objects.name: Voyager 1
objects.notes: start is AUTHORITATIVE (curated, day-after-launch so Horizons accepts it) -- confirm against the object definition. Coarse 7d glide backbone + daily densify inside the Jupiter (1979) and Saturn (1980) flyby windows + DP-prune of straight glides. No future fetched; nightly appends today's point.

objects.name: 2P/Encke
objects.notes: Tp-anchored conic. horizons_id is the specific Horizons record number (Rec #90000091, 2022-epoch solution), matching the orrery's proven Halley pattern (id='90000030') -- not the bare 'DES=2P' designation, which resolves ambiguously across 61 historical apparitions and is incompatible with closest_apparition under id_type='smallbody'. Verified live 2026-07-11. NOTE: this record is pinned -- won't auto-track a future JPL solution update; recheck periodically, same as Halley's pinned id.

objects.name: 1P/Halley
objects.notes: id='90000030' pinned to a specific Horizons record (1P/Halley), matching the pattern already proven for Encke (id='90000091'). Verified this session: Halley's ~76-year period means only one apparition is ever current (unlike Encke's ~3.3-year cadence, where a new record supersedes the last every few years) -- no live disambiguation search needed, this record is necessarily the current one. The orrery's own data-arc comment (1835-08-21 to 1994-01-11, celestial_objects.py) describes the observational fit-arc used to derive the elements, not a hard propagation cutoff -- Halley is an exceptionally well-characterized orbit. NOT yet live-verified against a 2026-epoch dry-run (no Horizons access from this session) -- run the routine --dry-run --object halley check before --first-build, same as any newly added object.
